author: Russell Brand
description:
Timothy Alberino describes his investigations into stories of giant skeletons on the island of Sardinia, where elderly locals told him that farmers began uncovering enormous bones after tractors became more common following World War II. Alberino says some of the remains were allegedly found alongside rings and necklaces, leading him to question whether they could simply be explained as prehistoric animal bones.

The conversation then turns to Sardinia’s megalithic structures and the so-called “Tombs of the Giants,” with Alberino claiming that skeletons measuring around 10 to 12 feet were uncovered at certain sites. From there, Russell connects the stories to ancient folklore like Gog and Magog and asks a deeper question: if myths persist across generations, could they be preserving fragments of something people once experienced as real?
